- `/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/docs/dev/herdr-hydrator.md` — Design + Safety sections need the second signal.
- `/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills/shared/work_item_lock.py` — producer of the lock protocol (`<worklog>/locks/child-<id>.lock`, metadata + `ENV_LOCK_TOKEN` re-entrancy); read-only contract for this fix.
- `/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills/implement/scripts/implement.py` — holds the lock for `phase_start`/`drive` lifetime (lines ~696–760); the population whose claims are being reverted.
- `/home/rgardler/projects/llm/.worklog/analysis/LP-0MVVG8BAT00238JK-hydrator-headless-demotion.md` — the dossier this item produces (analysis-doc convention already used in this store).
- `/home/rgardler/projects/llm/.worklog/logs/hydrator.log` — evidence source and its retention limit.

## Related work

**This store (`LP-`)** — `LP-0MVRMOV8K0007NFO` (*[verdict] AC3 closure verdict, successor link and rollback note*, discovered-from parent): the session whose claims were reverted three times.

**ContextHub store (`WL-`, the fix's home)** — verified present in `/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub`:

- `WL-0MSOJLZD9004P8PI` (completed) — *Herdr hydrator: rescue in_progress work items with no active pane*: the feature that introduced the demotion rule, plus `docs/dev/herdr-hydrator.md`.
- `WL-0MV1BWETT005GSUJ` (completed) — pane-title active-detection directive quoted in **Constraints** ("It should be simple …"), and the selection-list marker.
- `WL-0MTF5WO2Q008B8US` (completed) — *Hydrator: demote stale in_progress items*: AC3 defines the `open`/`intake_complete` release target.
- `WL-0MTTSWE0G008M1VA` (deleted, folded into `WL-0MSOJLZD9004P8PI`) — claim-age timeout: the "no pane ⇒ stale regardless of age" rule this defect qualifies.
- `WL-0MUY1CXSV008F8TZ` / `WL-0MUY1CYCB003DTKO` (completed) — per-step budgets and stdio isolation constraining the probe in **Constraints**.
- `WL-0MV25EE4E0028KDI` (completed) — hydrator docs/pane-title rationale, the doc to update.
- `WL-0MTWU4Y82001B3UH` (completed) — demotion audit-trail comment requirement (relevant to facet (a), stale `assignee`).
- `WL-0MSG4VSP10020NL7` (completed) — *Evaluate Pi subprocess mechanisms: headless `pi -p` vs herdr pane*: why driven sessions have no pane by design.

**Agent infrastructure (`SA-`)** — `SA-0MTFTFUIH000UWM9` (*actively worked ⇒ `in_progress`* invariant, the contract this violates); `SA-0MVOABYW00004978` (per-child lock rationale, `drive` duplicate-session RCA).

**Automated related-work report** (`find-related`, comment on this item) matched only proxy files in this repository — expected, since the hydrator and its tests live in ContextHub; those matches are noise and were not used.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — pid reuse.** A stale lock whose recorded pid now belongs to an unrelated process would suppress demotion indefinitely. Mitigation: require `started_at` ≤ process start time, or prefer the flock probe as authoritative; log the probe outcome.
- **Risk — cross-repo coupling.** The hydrator would depend on a lock format owned by the globally installed skills (SorraAgents). Mitigation: read it defensively (unknown/malformed ⇒ fail-open) and document the contract; or choose the worklog-native source (Appendix Q2, option C).
- **Risk — regression to stuck claims.** Suppression that outlives the holder re-creates `WL-0MSOJLZD9004P8PI`'s original defect. Mitigation: no TTL, kernel liveness only; explicit test for "dead holder ⇒ released".
- **Risk — evidence loss.** `hydrator.log` keeps only the live window with no rotation, so the dossier must capture its evidence at writing time (AC2); longer retention is recorded as a separate opportunity, not scope.
- **Risk — partial observation.** Facet (c) ("herdr pane whose pane id changed was released") is *reported but not reproduced*; the dossier must label it as such rather than assert it.
- **Assumption.** A driven child session's `implement.py` lock is held for the whole session lifetime (verified in `implement.py` around `_set_child_lock` / `phase_start`), so it is a faithful "session is alive" proxy.
- **Assumption.** Patch-level verification will happen in the ContextHub store; this item is validated by dossier quality (AC7), not by a green hydrator test run here.
- **Risk — scope creep.** Drive-orchestrator redesign, hydrator log rotation and `assignee`-clearing on release are adjacent opportunities; they are recorded as facets/candidates, not implemented under this item.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (scope/home).** "Should this item stay report-only, or should it also raise the implementation item in the ContextHub store?" — **OPEN QUESTION** (no producer answer yet; asked by `intake` agent in a `wl comment`, 2026-10-31). Options: (A) report-only, as currently drafted; (B) report here **plus** create a `WL-` implementation item in `/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub` cross-referencing this one; (C) implement the hydrator fix from an `LP-` worktree (crosses repositories — not supported by the worktree-isolation rules). **Recommended: B** — the code, tests and docs all live in ContextHub, so the fix needs an owner in that store, while this item remains the evidence record. Research: `rg -l "no matching pane" ~/projects` shows the hydrator only in `ContextHub/packages/herdr/**` and its docs.
- **Q2 (claim signal).** "Which pane-less claim signal should the hydrator honour?" — **OPEN QUESTION**. Options: (A) the existing per-child lock (`<worklog>/locks/child-<id>.lock`), probed for *heldness* via non-blocking `flock` with pid-liveness fallback; (B) a new worklog-native claim record (claim token/assignee convention or refreshed comment) written by `implement.py`; (C) a registered herdr "virtual pane"/pane-title entry for driven sessions. **Recommended: A** — kernel-authoritative, no new protocol, no TTL, and already covers exactly the `drive`/`phase`/`start` population; research shows all 40 existing lock files are stale, so heldness (not existence) is mandatory.
- **Q3 (stale assignee).** "When the hydrator releases a claim, should it also clear `assignee` (releasing the scheduling hold)?" — **OPEN QUESTION**. Options: (A) yes, clear `assignee` on release (a released item should not stay parked); (B) no, preserve it as diagnostic evidence of who last held the claim; (C) clear only when the release is a stale-claim release, never on the `in_review`/`blocked` branches. **Recommended: A with a comment** — the workflow treats any non-empty assignee as a scheduling hold, so a released item that keeps one is undispatachable; recording the previous holder in the release comment preserves the diagnostic value. Research: live example `LP-0MVUH9OMY004MQ3U` is `open/intake_complete` with `assignee=Map` after its 04:36:31Z release, and `applyDemotion` (`hydrator.ts:1030`) passes only `--status`/`--stage`.

_Questions were recorded on the work item as a `wl comment` and the item flagged `needs-producer-review`; the intake deliverable above stands on the stated recommended options until the producer answers._

# Validate writer-side sidecar pairing fix — >=24 h post-deploy window (earliest = deploy + 24 h)

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want a >=24 h post-deploy window proving the fixed
snapshot/sidecar directory pairing makes the restored-prefix credit fire, so
AC3 of LP-0MVVI8TEU006KTOZ (and AC3 of LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E) can be answered
with real numbers instead of the pre-fix 0 found / 0 restored baseline.

## Scheduling (read first)

**Do not start before the deployed fix has been live for 24 h.** The proxy is
deployed by restarting it from the main checkout (`/skill:start-proxy
--restart`) after this fix's commit is on `dev`. Record the restart timestamp
(uvicorn start time) here when it happens; the earliest valid measurement is
**restart timestamp + 24 h**. Extend the window rather than concluding early.
Keep the `Map` assignee as the scheduling hold until the window is valid.

## Background

The pre-fix measurement (LP-0MVTJVNSO008IZEB, 2026-10-29T12:58:32Z ..
2026-10-30T12:58:32Z) found 605 `missing_sidecar` seeds, 0 `found`, 0
`cache_state=restored` dispatches. LP-0MVVI8TEU006KTOZ identified the cause:
llama-server writes `<--slot-save-path>/<basename>` (it rejects subdirectories)
while the proxy wrote the `.ratio.json` sidecar and checked restore under
`<root>/{host}-{port}/`. The fix makes save/restore/sidecar/seed all use the
shared root (an eviction save with no recorded prefix still saves its snapshot
but writes no sidecar, as documented in LP-0MVK0E80C009HUQC).

Evidence for the pre-fix state:
`docs/dev/slot-sidecar-pairing-fix-LP-0MVVI8TEU006KTOZ.md`,
`docs/dev/slot-sidecar-attribution-LP-0MVVI8TEU006KTOZ.json`,
`docs/dev/slot-ratio-restore-postfix-2026-10-30.md`.

## Procedure

1. Confirm the deployed tree contains the fix commit (`git log -1 dev`);
   confirm no proxy restart inside the window (a restart resets in-memory
   ratios; note it if it happens).
2. Run the measurement tool over the post-deploy window and an equal-length
   pre-deploy window, with pinned timestamps:

   ```bash
   python3 scripts/analyse_slot_ratio_restore.py \
     --log-dir /var/log/llama-proxy \
     --slot-cache-dir /home/rgardler/projects/llm/slot-cache \
     --window "post-fix=<deploy>,<deploy+24h>" \
     --window "pre-fix=<deploy-24h>,<deploy>" \
     --json > docs/dev/slot-ratio-restore-postfix-<date>.json
   ```

3. Attribute any remaining `missing_sidecar` seeds:

   ```bash
   python3 scripts/attribute_missing_sidecar.py \
     --log-dir /var/log/llama-proxy \
     --window "<deploy>,<deploy+24h>" --json
   ```

4. On-disk pairing: every `slot_*.bin` must have its `.ratio.json` in the same
   directory; no orphan growth for snapshots saved after the deploy:

   ```bash
   cd /home/rgardler/projects/llm/slot-cache
   echo "snapshots=$(find . -name '*.bin' | wc -l) sidecars=$(find . -name '*.bin.ratio.json' | wc -l)"
   find . -name '*.bin' -exec basename {} \; | sed 's/\.bin$//' | sort > /tmp/snaps
   find . -name '*.bin.ratio.json' -exec basename {} \; | sed 's/\.bin\.ratio\.json$//' | sort > /tmp/sides
   comm -13 /tmp/snaps /tmp/sides | wc -l   # orphan sidecars
   comm -23 /tmp/snaps /tmp/sides | wc -l   # orphan snapshots
   ```

5. State restored-vs-cold `dispatch_first_byte_ms` p50/p90 in the same context
   bucket, with sample counts.
6. Write the report under `docs/dev/` with the exact commands and JSON
   artifact, and link it from LP-0MVVI8TEU006KTOZ and LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E.
7. If restored dispatches are still zero, say so honestly, explain the
   outcome counts, and file a follow-up instead of claiming success.

## Expected post-fix signature

- `slot_ratio_seed outcome=found` > 0 and `slot_ratio_restored` events > 0.
- `cache_state=restored` dispatches > 0.
- `missing_sidecar` near 0 for sessions saved after the deploy; any residual
  should be attributable with `scripts/attribute_missing_sidecar.py` (an
  eviction save with no recorded prefix still produces an unpaired snapshot).
- `missing_snapshot` may appear for legacy orphan sidecars until
  retirement/`scripts/cleanup-slot-cache.sh` clears them.
- `prefix_mismatch` / `expired` become *possible*: a non-zero count is the
  success signal that the guard now runs; do not "fix" it.

## Acceptance criteria

- A post-deploy window of >=24 h contains more than zero `cache_state=restored` dispatches and more than zero `slot_ratio_seed outcome=found` events, with exact counts stated.
- On-disk pairing at report time shows paired files in the same directory and no orphan growth for snapshots saved after the deploy, with counts.
- `missing_sidecar` counts for the window are stated and are ~0 for post-deploy sessions; any residual is attributed with the raw counts.
- `dispatch_first_byte_ms` p50/p90 for restored dispatches are stated against cold dispatches in the same context bucket, with sample counts for both groups.
- A written report with the exact command line and a JSON artifact is added under `docs/dev/` and linked from LP-0MVVI8TEU006KTOZ and LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E.
- If restored dispatches are still zero, the verdict says so honestly, explains the outcome counts, and files a follow-up item instead of claiming success.

- Post-fix ≥24 h window after the NEW deploy shows `outcome=found` > 0 and `cache_state=restored` dispatches > 0 (matching LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E AC3), or a documented, evidence-backed explanation of why the credit cannot fire with the current guard/prefix semantics.

## Risks / notes

- Snapshot-bearing traffic is thin (617 seed decisions in the pre-fix 24 h); if
  the post-deploy window yields too few restored samples, extend it rather
  than concluding early.
- Legacy orphan sidecars in `{host}-{port}/` predate the fix; the success
  signal is no orphan growth for **sessions saved after the deploy**, not an
  absolute zero.
- Do not credit local-prefill movement to this path unless `found`/`restored`
  are non-zero.

## Traceability

- discovered-from: LP-0MVVI8TEU006KTOZ (writer-side sidecar pairing fix)
- covers AC3 of LP-0MVVI8TEU006KTOZ
- answers AC3 of LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E
- validates: the fix committed by LP-0MVVI8TEU006KTOZ
- baseline: `docs/dev/slot-sidecar-pairing-fix-LP-0MVVI8TEU006KTOZ.md`,
  `docs/dev/slot-sidecar-attribution-LP-0MVVI8TEU006KTOZ.json`

## Key Files

- `scripts/analyse_slot_ratio_restore.py` — windows, `cache_state` tables, bucket pairs, `seed_outcomes`.
- `scripts/attribute_missing_sidecar.py` — per-write-path `missing_sidecar` attribution.
- `docs/dev/slot-sidecar-pairing-fix-LP-0MVVI8TEU006KTOZ.md` — the fix + pre-fix evidence.
- `/var/log/llama-proxy` — source logs.
- `/home/rgardler/projects/llm/slot-cache` — snapshot/sidecar inventory.

# Land the snapshot/sidecar path-alignment fix on dev

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the already-diagnosed path-alignment fix merged to `dev`
and deployable, so that a snapshot saved by llama-server is paired with its
`.ratio.json` sidecar and the restored-prefix credit can actually fire.

## Background

The parent (LP-0MVVI8TEU006KTOZ) established the root cause with 24 h of
evidence (see `docs/dev/slot-sidecar-pairing-fix-LP-0MVVI8TEU006KTOZ.md` and
`docs/dev/slot-sidecar-attribution-LP-0MVVI8TEU006KTOZ.json` on the work
branch): llama-server accepts only a bare filename
(`fs_validate_filename(..., allow_subdirs=false)`) and writes
`<--slot-save-path>/<basename>`, while commit `bb4c2d44` made the proxy believe
the snapshot lived in a `{host}-{port}/` subdirectory. Snapshot at the root,
sidecar one directory down → every seed reported `missing_sidecar`, the restore
existence pre-check short-circuited, 0 `found` / 0 `cache_state=restored`.

The fix is implemented and not yet merged: branch
`wl-LP-0MVVI8TEU006KTOZ-writer-side-sidecar-still-absent-at-seed`, commit
`dd171423` ("Implementation complete"), based on `2cdf864b`. `dev` has since
moved to `c861fe32` and the earlier push was rejected (non-fast-forward), so the
remaining work is to rebase, re-verify and land it.

## Scope

**In scope** (all present in `dd171423`, to be preserved through the rebase):

- `proxy/proxy/session.py` — `_build_slot_context` keeps the shared
  `session_slot_save_path` root (no `{host}-{port}` suffix); eviction save
  gated on a resolvable recorded prefix (`_eviction_sidecar_source`), with
  `slot_save … saved=False source=eviction pairing=no_sidecar_source` when the
  gate closes.
- `proxy/proxy/slot_cache_ratio.py` — `_candidate_slot_filenames` tries the
  root first and keeps `{host}-{port}/` as a legacy read/retire fallback.
- Docs: `proxy/README.md`, `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md`, `proxy/config.yaml` (the
  multi-backend and `session_slot_save_path` comments) describe the shared root
  and the requirement that every local llama-server's `--slot-save-path` points
  at `session_slot_save_path`.
- `scripts/attribute_missing_sidecar.py` + `tests/test_attribute_missing_sidecar.py`
  (AC1 attribution tool) and the four new tests in
  `proxy/tests/test_slot_cache_ratio_restore.py`
  (`test_slot_context_uses_the_llama_server_save_directory`,
  `test_router_save_is_seedable_where_llama_server_wrote_it`,
  `test_legacy_endpoint_directory_snapshot_still_seeds`,
  `test_no_recorded_prefix_writes_no_snapshot_or_sidecar`).
- `docs/dev/slot-sidecar-pairing-fix-LP-0MVVI8TEU006KTOZ.md` (AC1/AC4 verdict,
  exact commands) and its JSON artifact.

**Out of scope:** the writer-skip log line for the router path and the retire
pairing tests (sibling item "Pin pairing invariants and log sidecar write
skips"); save-failure tuning (sibling item "Triage the slot-save failure
cliff"); the ≥24 h post-deploy measurement (existing item
LP-0MVVLQMG1000843Q). Do **not** restart the proxy from this item — the restart
starts the validation clock.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/session.py`
- `proxy/proxy/slot_cache_ratio.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_slot_cache_ratio_restore.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_multi_backend.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_slot_pool_sizing_doc.py`
- `proxy/README.md`
- `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md`
- `proxy/config.yaml`
- `scripts/attribute_missing_sidecar.py`
- `tests/test_attribute_missing_sidecar.py`
- `docs/dev/slot-sidecar-pairing-fix-LP-0MVVI8TEU006KTOZ.md`

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (rebase).** The work branch is rebased onto current `dev`; the diff
  against `dev` contains only the intended fix/doc/tool files, and no unrelated
  dev commit is reverted (`git diff --stat dev...HEAD` reviewed).
- **AC2 (gate).** Build plus the changed-scope suite are green through the test
  skill (`/skill:test`), including the four restore tests above and
  `proxy/tests/test_multi_backend.py`.
- **AC3 (landed).** The fix is pushed to `dev`; the merge commit hash and the
  branch name are recorded in a comment on the parent.
- **AC4 (pairing proof).** A test demonstrates the server-side behaviour the fix
  relies on — llama-server writes `<root>/slot_<session>.bin` from a basename —
  and that the `.ratio.json` sidecar lands beside it, so a subsequent seed can
  reach `outcome=found` rather than `missing_sidecar`.
- **AC5 (verdict doc + attribution).** `docs/dev/slot-sidecar-pairing-fix-LP-0MVVI8TEU006KTOZ.md`
  is updated to state the merged commit hash, the deploy requirement (every
  local llama-server's `--slot-save-path` == `session_slot_save_path`), and
  that parent AC3 is time-gated on LP-0MVVLQMG1000843Q (measurement only after
  deploy + 24 h). It also carries parent AC1: the per-write-path attribution of
  the 24 h post-fix `missing_sidecar` seeds (eviction 414 / router 181 /
  no-save-in-window 10 of 605) with the exact `attribute_missing_sidecar.py`
  command line and the committed JSON artifact.
- **AC6 (no orphan regression).** On the landed tree, a snapshot written by a
  post-fix save has its sidecar beside it in the cache root, and legacy
  `{host}-{port}/` orphans are still discovered and retired (verified by test
  or by a dry-run of `scripts/cleanup-slot-cache.sh`).
- A minimal repro or direct log evidence pins which write path produced each observed `missing_sidecar` snapshot (router vs eviction), with counts for at least the 24 h post-fix window.
- Root cause identified and fixed so that a snapshot saved post-fix is paired with a sidecar (AC6-style pairing check: paired files present, no orphan growth for post-deploy saves).
- Verdict recorded in `docs/dev/` with exact command line and JSON artifact mirroring LP-0MVTJVNSO008IZEB.

## Parent AC mapping

The last three bullets above are the parent acceptance criteria this item
closes, restated verbatim from LP-0MVVI8TEU006KTOZ so tree coverage is
machine-checkable: parent AC1 (write-path attribution), parent AC2 (root cause
fixed + pairing), parent AC4 (verdict recorded). Parent AC3 (>=24 h post-deploy
`found`/`restored` > 0) is closed by the child item LP-0MVVLQMG1000843Q.

## Notes

- Deploying is a separate, explicit step (`/skill:start-proxy --restart`) owned
  by LP-0MVVLQMG1000843Q, which must record the restart timestamp before the
  24 h window can begin.
- The main checkout currently carries an unrelated dirty file
  (`proxy/tests/test_abandoned_local_dispatch.py`); leave it untouched.

# Pin pairing invariants and log sidecar write skips

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the snapshot↔sidecar contract pinned by tests and every
skipped sidecar write visible in the logs, so a future writer-side regression is
caught before deployment and attributable from logs instead of being inferred
from seed outcomes.

## Background

The re-measurement comment on the parent (2026-10-31T04:36Z) recommends three
writer-side invariants; two are implemented on the fix branch and one is not:

1. retire/cleanup removes the snapshot and sidecar as a unit — implemented
   (`session._retire_slot_snapshot`, `_retire_session_slot_snapshots`), but no
   dedicated test proves both files disappear in either direction;
2. `_write_eviction_sidecar` never leaves a snapshot without a sidecar when a
   recorded prefix exists — implemented (eviction save is gated and logs
   `pairing=no_sidecar_source`), test present
   (`test_no_recorded_prefix_writes_no_snapshot_or_sidecar`);
3. when a sidecar genuinely cannot be written, log a
   `slot_sidecar_write_skipped reason=…` line — **not implemented on the router
   path**: `proxy/proxy/router.py` (~line 747) calls
   `write_slot_ratio_sidecar` only when `sidecar_cached_tokens() > 0` and
   otherwise returns silently, so a 0-token fallback leaves an unseedable
   snapshot with no log evidence at all.

## Scope

**In scope:** the router-path skip log line (behaviour-neutral, INFO), tests that
pin each pairing invariant, and a short docs note for the new log line.
**Out of scope:** changing any token-counting, threshold, guard or restore
behaviour; the path-alignment fix itself (sibling item "Land the snapshot/
sidecar path-alignment fix on dev", which this item builds on); save-failure
tuning (sibling item "Triage the slot-save failure cliff").

Tests are written first and their failing-first evidence recorded in a comment
before the logging change is committed.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/router.py`
- `proxy/proxy/session.py`
- `proxy/proxy/slot_cache_ratio.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_slot_cache_ratio_restore.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_multi_backend.py`
- `proxy/README.md`

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (test-first).** The new tests are committed before the logging change in
  this item, with the failing-first run recorded in a comment (the skip-line
  assertion fails because the line does not exist yet).
- **AC2 (router skip is observable).** When `sidecar_cached_tokens()` returns 0,
  the router save path emits one INFO line
  `slot_sidecar_write_skipped reason=no_trustworthy_count source=router …`
  carrying the session prefix, slot id and the model; a unit test pins it.
- **AC3 (router success unchanged).** With `sidecar_cached_tokens() > 0` the
  sidecar is still written beside the snapshot and no skip line is emitted; a
  unit test pins both halves.
- **AC4 (eviction gate pinned).** A test asserts the eviction path emits
  `saved=False source=eviction pairing=no_sidecar_source` and creates no
  snapshot file when the session has no recorded prefix.
- **AC5 (retire pairing pinned).** A test asserts retirement removes the
  snapshot **and** its sidecar together, for the root layout and for a legacy
  `{host}-{port}/` layout, leaving no orphan in either direction.
- **AC6 (round trip pinned).** An end-to-end unit test proves save → sidecar
  beside the snapshot → `slot_ratio_seed outcome=found` → restore pre-check
  finds the snapshot (no `missing_sidecar`, no short-circuit).
- **AC7 (docs).** `proxy/README.md` slot-persistence/retention section documents
  the skip log line and its `reason` vocabulary (`no_trustworthy_count`).
- **AC8 (gate).** Changed-scope suite is green through the test skill
  (`/skill:test`).

## Notes

- Logging must stay behaviour-neutral: no branch, threshold, credited value or
  save/restore decision may change (same rule as LP-0MVJYZWWW005XGW7).
- Do not "fix" a non-zero `prefix_mismatch`/`expired` if one appears during
  verification — those are the success signal that the seed path runs past
  lookup (parent notes).

# Triage the slot-save failure cliff

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the 66–67 % router-path slot-save failure rate
(`ReadTimeout` plus `slot_busy` skips) attributed to a specific cause and either
fixed or split into an evidence-backed follow-up, so that sidecar supply is no
longer starved independently of the snapshot-path fix.

## Background

Parent hypothesis 4 ("Save-failure cliff"). Measured on the parent's window
(`2026-10-29T12:58:32Z → 2026-10-31T04:09:00Z`, 39.17 h post-fix):

- router-path slot saves **46 ok / 94 failed (67.1 % fail)**, up from
  103/33 (24 % fail) pre-fix; eviction saves 42/64;
- `slot persistence skipped reason=slot_busy` **375** (155 pre-fix, 260 in the
  first 24 h);
- `ReadTimeout` dominates the failures (52 of 106 `slot_save` failures).

A failing save writes no sidecar, so this reduces supply even after the
path-alignment fix lands. It is unknown whether the cause is timeout tuning
(`session_slot_timeout_seconds` default 3.0 s, optional per-token scaling via
`session_slot_timeout_per_token_seconds` / `session_slot_max_timeout_seconds`),
concurrency (slot contention → `slot_busy`), or a llama-server-side regression
(save latency growth). It must be decided with evidence, not guessed.

## Scope

**In scope:** measurement + attribution of the failures, the decision, and — if
the evidence points at a proxy-side timeout or skip policy — the smallest
targeted change with a test. **Out of scope:** the snapshot/sidecar path fix
(sibling item "Land the snapshot/sidecar path-alignment fix on dev") and the
≥24 h post-deploy restored-prefix measurement (LP-0MVVLQMG1000843Q), which this
item must not block.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/session.py` (slot save path, timeout derivation, `slot_busy` skip)
- `proxy/config.yaml` (`session_slot_timeout_seconds`,
  `session_slot_timeout_per_token_seconds`,
  `session_slot_max_timeout_seconds`, `session_slot_pool_size`)
- `scripts/attribute_missing_sidecar.py`
- `scripts/analyse_slot_ratio_restore.py`
- `docs/dev/`

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (measurement).** A documented command line plus committed JSON artifact
  in `docs/dev/` quantify, for a stated ≥24 h window: save attempts per path
  (router / eviction), ok vs failed, failure reasons (`ReadTimeout` etc.),
  `slot persistence skipped reason=…` counts, and — if the logs carry it — the
  save-duration distribution; if duration is not logged, say so explicitly
  rather than estimating it.
- **AC2 (hypothesis verdicts).** Each of the three hypotheses (timeout too short
  for large snapshots / slot contention / llama-server-side regression) is
  marked **supported** or **refuted** with the specific evidence that decides
  it, including the snapshot-size and concurrency correlates where computable.
- **AC3 (decision).** A decision is recorded: either a minimal fix is
  implemented with a test, or follow-up work items are created (ids recorded,
  with the blocking relation to this item) — no silently deferred cliff.
- **AC4 (supply impact).** The report states what share of
  `missing_sidecar`/`missing_snapshot` seeds is attributable to a failed save, so
  parent AC3 can be interpreted correctly if `found` stays low after the fix.
- **AC5 (no masking).** No tuning value is changed without naming both the old
  and new deployed value and the measurement that justifies it; the changed-scope
  suite is green through the test skill if code changes.

## Notes

- Run the measurement through the test/analysis scripts as documented; do not
  hand-edit JSON artifacts.
- If the cause is llama-server-side, file the follow-up against the server
  configuration (e.g. `models.ini` / `start-proxy.sh`) rather than the proxy.

data.description:
# slots_500_triage.py: progress-dot artifact causes child 503 lines to report as unknown

## Problem

`scripts/slots_500_triage.py`'s `_ACCESS_RE` regex fails to match `GET /slots` access lines that are physically prefixed with the tail of a llama-server progress-dot line (no newline between dots and the access line). Example:

```text
[60965] .......................srv  log_server_r: done request: GET /slots 127.0.0.1 503
```

The regex expects `\s*` after the optional `[pid]` but encounters `.` characters instead, so the line is reported as `unknown:?` rather than being attributed to child `60965:503`. The live corpus contains **9** such lines versus **17** correctly attributed child 503s — a ~35% undercount of child-503 events.

## Users

- SRE/on-call engineers running the triage tool during incident response (F3 workflow).
- Automated audits (e.g. LP-0MVU7ZYLR0044D12) that depend on accurate responder splits.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Regex tolerates leading dots.** `_ACCESS_RE` matches lines where `.` characters appear between the optional `[pid]` bracket and the `srv` keyword (e.g. `[.\s]*` instead of `\s*`). Verified against the example: `[60965] .......................srv  log_server_r: done request: GET /slots 127.0.0.1 503` → matches with `pid=60965`, `status=503`.
- **AC2 — No regression on clean lines.** All existing corpus lines and the F3/incident fixtures (including `llama-server.log-2026-08-27.gz`) produce identical responder splits and counter values — no change to reported numbers.
- **AC3 — Tests.** `proxy/tests/test_slots_500_triage.py` includes a test case driving a log fixture with progress-dot-prefixed 503 lines and asserts correct pid attribution (not `unknown`).
- **AC4 — Live corpus verification.** Running the triage tool on the live corpus now attributes all 9 previously-unparsed child-503 lines, bringing the child-503 count to the full 26.

## Constraints

- Do not change the responder classification logic (`router` = no `[pid]`, otherwise child pid).
- The fix is limited to `_ACCESS_RE` only — no other regexes or parsing logic.
- The dot artifact only appears on 503 lines in the current corpus, so the risk to other status codes is nil.

## Existing state

- `_ACCESS_RE` at `scripts/slots_500_triage.py:49` uses `\s*` between the optional `[pid]` and `srv`.
- Parent item LP-0MVVWTWGY004BO5H deliberately left `_ACCESS_RE` unchanged to keep that fix surgical.

## Desired change

Replace `\s*` with `[.\s]*` (or equivalent) in the `_ACCESS_RE` pattern to tolerate leading dot characters before `srv`.

## Key Files

- `scripts/slots_500_triage.py` — `_ACCESS_RE` definition (~line 49)
- `proxy/tests/test_slots_500_triage.py` — extend with dot-prefixed fixture test
- `scripts/slots_500_triage.py` — `analyze_slots_500` responder split (~line 112)

## Related work

- **LP-0MVVWTWGY004BO5H** — *slots_500_triage.py crashes on any /slots 503 response* — parent: fixes the KeyError crash; deliberately does not touch `_ACCESS_RE`.
- **LP-0MVP7HV7Q001AJF8** — Epic parent covering the router-responder 400/500 verification work.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk:** The regex change could match unintended lines if dots appear in other contexts. **Mitigation:** Only 503 lines in the corpus carry this artifact; the pattern `[.\s]*` is narrow enough to not cause false matches elsewhere.
- **Assumption:** The dot artifact is caused by llama-server's in-place progress-dot output not being flushed with a newline before the access log line; this is a known llama-server behaviour (hybrid-arch checkpoint re-prefill).
- **Risk:** Low. This is a minor data-quality fix with a small, well-contained code change.

## Scope Creep

- Improving the llama-server log format or fixing the dot artifact at the source is out of scope for this work item.

# Goal

Author the **red-first** test suite that encodes the new `/slots` read-path contract *before* any
implementation, so every implementation child in this plan is driven by failing tests rather than
written first and tested afterwards.

These tests pin the behaviour that makes `slots_stale` measurable and small: one bounded upstream
fetch per refresh cycle, a snapshot-age freshness definition, and untouched reconciliation
guarantees for `capacity_hint`.

# Test matrix

1. **Fan-out.** N concurrent `GET /llama/local/status` polls inside the freshness window issue
   **exactly one** upstream `/slots` request. Extend the existing coalescing suite rather than
   writing a second harness.
2. **Latency bound.** With an injected backend that never answers, the status handler returns
   within the configured budget (`STATUS_QUERY_TIMEOUT`) plus a small slack — it must not serialise
   counts (2 s) + detail (1 s) + status (1 s) awaits.
3. **Age-derived freshness.** A table-driven test asserts `slots_stale` follows the published
   snapshot age versus the freshness budget: `age < budget ⇒ false`, `age == budget ⇒ false`,
   `age > budget ⇒ true`, and `missing snapshot ⇒ true`.
4. **Additive schema.** A consumer that ignores unknown fields sees unchanged `available_slots` /
   `total_slots` / `slots` semantics; the payload carries the versioned schema field.
5. **Stale reconciliation unchanged.** For every stale-snapshot fixture, `capacity_hint` is never
   `saturated` while `local_in_flight_requests == 0` (LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM AC3 must survive this
   change).
6. **Log compatibility.** The `status_request` line gains per-phase timing fields additively;
   the existing parsers (`scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py`,
   `proxy/tests/test_status_logging.py`) keep parsing unchanged lines.

# Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The new/updated tests exist and **fail (red)** against current `dev` for the fan-out,
  latency-bound and age-derivation assertions, and the failing run summary is recorded on this item.
- AC2: The fan-out test asserts an exact upstream call count of 1 for 5 concurrent polls inside the
  freshness window (not a `<=` bound).
- AC3: The hang-injection test asserts handler wall-clock latency `< budget + 250 ms` when `/slots`
  never responds.
- AC4: The age-derivation table covers `< budget`, `== budget`, `> budget` and missing-snapshot
  cases, one assertion each.
- AC5: Stale-reconciliation regression tests assert `capacity_hint != "saturated"` whenever
  `local_in_flight_requests == 0` across all stale fixtures.
- AC6: The suite goes green after the implementation children land **without editing these tests**
  (no test rewrites to chase the implementation).

# Key Files:

- `proxy/tests/test_slots_poll_coalescing.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_llama_local_status.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_slots_detail_cache_fallback.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_status_logging.py`

# Reuse

- Existing coalescing/single-flight harness (`_fetch_slots_payload`, LP-0MUCEFD5B003TURT tests).
- Existing stale-reconciliation fixtures in `test_slots_detail_cache_fallback.py`.

# Goal

Publish **per-phase timing and provenance** for the `/slots` read path so the dominant contributor
to stale (> 2 s) refreshes is measured from the log instead of inferred (parent AC1). Today the
`status_request` line carries only an aggregate `latency_ms`, so a stale poll cannot be attributed
to the counts query, the detail query, the status query, or to a cache path.

# Fields (additive, `status_request` line)

- `status_query_ms` — the `query_llama_status()` phase.
- `slots_counts_ms` — the counts query phase (`null` when not attempted).
- `slots_detail_ms` — the per-slot detail phase (`null` when not attempted).
- `slots_upstream_calls` — how many upstream `/slots` fetches this poll caused (0 or 1 today).
- `slots_snapshot_age_seconds` — age of the snapshot the poll was served from (`null` when none).
- `slots_snapshot_source` — one of `upstream` | `snapshot` | `ttl_cache` | `failure_backoff` |
  `none`.

No existing field is renamed, reordered or removed; the payload schema version is bumped by the
later freshness-semantics child, not here.

# Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: Every `status_request` line carries all seven new fields, each an integer/float or `null`,
  never absent (asserted by test for the success, timeout and backend-down paths).
- AC2: `slots_snapshot_source` correctly labels an upstream fetch, a TTL-cache hit and a
  failure-backoff hit, one fixture each.
- AC3: Phase timings reconcile on a fixture with known values:
  `status_query_ms + slots_counts_ms + slots_detail_ms <= latency_ms`.
- AC4: Existing log consumers still parse unchanged lines — the analysis tool's field regex and
  `test_status_logging.py` are extended, not broken (regression test).
- AC5: No behavioural change to the payload verdicts: the full existing slots/status test files
  pass unchanged.

# Key Files:

- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py`
- `proxy/proxy/observability.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_status_logging.py`
- `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py`

# Reuse

- The handler already computes `_latency_ms`; phase stamps are `time.monotonic()` deltas around
  the existing awaits.
- `_cached_slots_payload()` already knows whether a payload came from the TTL cache or the
  failure backoff — expose that decision instead of re-deriving it.

# Goal

Stop the status endpoint from **blocking on a synchronous `/slots` fetch**. Today
`get_llama_local_status()` performs its own counts query (2 s budget) *and* its own detail query
(`STATUS_QUERY_TIMEOUT`, 1 s budget) in series, even though the periodic refresher already queries
`/slots` every 1 s and stamps `_last_slot_details_at`. That duplication doubles upstream load and
couples poll latency — and therefore `slots_stale` — to llama-server's slowest path.

# Design (smallest end-to-end slice)

- One shared snapshot provider: a single `/slots` fetch path produces `(counts, per-slot detail,
  fetched_at)`; counts and detail are derived from **the same payload**, so they can never disagree.
- The status handler serves that snapshot; it performs at most one bounded fresh fetch per poll and
  only when the snapshot is missing or older than the freshness budget.
- The refresher keeps a bounded timeout; a slow backend degrades to the previous snapshot instead of
  extending the poll.
- All existing payload contracts hold: `slots` annotation (`lease_state`, `phase`, ETA), the
  empty-array fallback, `capacity_hint` reconciliation, `SLOT_COUNTS_STALE_AFTER_SECONDS`.

# Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: A status poll causes at most one upstream `/slots` fetch and reuses the shared snapshot when
  it is within the freshness budget (asserted by exact call count in tests).
- AC2: Handler wall-clock latency stays within budget (`STATUS_QUERY_TIMEOUT` + 250 ms slack) when
  the backend hangs, verified by the hang-injection test.
- AC3: `available_slots`/`total_slots` and the per-slot `is_processing` values are always derived
  from one payload — a single-source test proves they cannot disagree.
- AC4: Payload parity: `slots`, `available_slots`, `total_slots`, annotation fields and
  `capacity_hint` are unchanged for consumers on equivalent backend data (parity test).
- AC5: Failure paths stay well-formed: empty snapshot ⇒ `slots: []`; snapshot older than
  `SLOT_COUNTS_STALE_AFTER_SECONDS` ⇒ counts fail closed (never served as current capacity).

# Key Files:

- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py`
- `proxy/proxy/observability.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_slots_poll_coalescing.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_llama_local_status.py`

# Reuse

- `_fetch_slots_payload()` already provides TTL caching plus single-flight (LP-0MUCEFD5B003TURT).
- `_last_slot_details_cache` / `_last_slot_details_at` already carry a stamped snapshot.
- `_resolve_slot_details_for_enrichment()` already keeps the cache pristine against log-derived data.

# Goal

Make `slots_stale` **measure staleness**, not cache use. Once the poll path serves a warm snapshot
by design, "served from cache" is true for almost every poll and the metric stops meaning anything.
Define freshness by the age of the snapshot the poll was served from, publish that age, and derive
`slots_stale` from it.

# Design

- Freshness budget: `SLOTS_SNAPSHOT_MAX_AGE_SECONDS` (env, default `2.0` = two refresher cycles).
- Payload gains `slot_snapshot_age_seconds` and `slots_snapshot_source`; `status_schema_version`
  moves to `5`. Additive: a consumer ignoring them is unaffected.
- `slots_stale` = `slot_snapshot_age_seconds > SLOTS_SNAPSHOT_MAX_AGE_SECONDS` (including the
  missing-snapshot case). `slots_detail_stale` keeps its current meaning for `capacity_hint`
  reconciliation; `slot_counts_stale` keeps its meaning for the counts fallback.
- Snapshot age is stamped from the **successful fetch** time on a monotonic clock, never from the
  poll's read time (the LP-0MVECWYWK000U3E1 lesson: never re-stamp stale data as fresh).
- The analysis surfaces (`scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py`, nightly report producer) read
  the new fields.

# Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: `slots_stale=true` if and only if the served snapshot age exceeds
  `SLOTS_SNAPSHOT_MAX_AGE_SECONDS`; the age is published in the payload and on the `status_request`
  line (table-driven test: `< budget`, `== budget`, `> budget`, no snapshot).
- AC2: Schema `5` is additive — a consumer ignoring the new fields observes unchanged behaviour, and
  the version bump is asserted by the contract test.
- AC3: Snapshot age is monotonic-clock derived from the successful fetch, never negative, never
  reset by a cache read (a frozen-backend fixture must show the age growing monotonically).
- AC4: `capacity_hint` reconciliation still keys on `slots_detail_stale` and still yields no
  `saturated` while `local_in_flight_requests == 0` — all existing reconciliation tests pass
  unchanged.
- AC5: `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py` reports `slots_stale` from the new definition and
  tolerates old-schema windows (pre-change lines without the age field are counted as before), with
  tests.
- AC6: The freshness-semantics decision is recorded on the parent with producer confirmation via
  `wl reviewed`, or the implementer records the explicit acceptance of the plan's recommended option
  (Appendix Q1) before coding.

# Key Files:

- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py`
- `proxy/proxy/observability.py`
- `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_llama_local_status.py`
- `proxy/docs/per-slot-status-verification.md`

# Reuse

- `_last_slot_details_at` already stamps the last successful fetch.
- `_latency_band` / attribution output in the analysis tool accepts additive fields.

## Goal

Write the failing tests for the **release→backend-cancel joiner** before it
exists, so "the proxy released a dispatch and llama-server kept prefilling"
becomes a measured, per-dispatch fact instead of the subtraction of two
unrelated counters.

Parent: LP-0MVVEQW5Y00962T2 — AC2 (and the instrument AC1 needs).

## Target outcome

A hermetic fixture pair (a proxy-log slice plus the matching
`llama-server.log` slice) and a test module that pin the joiner's contract.
The tests fail until the implementation item lands.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Fixture pair is committed and hermetic.** `proxy/tests/fixtures/`
  holds a proxy-log slice and a `llama-server.log` slice covering the same
  fake window, containing all four shapes: (a) release → backend cancel → N
  `prompt processing progress` lines → `slot release: … stop processing`;
  (b) release with **no** observed backend cancel; (c) release whose cancel
  exists but cannot be joined to a task id; (d) a cancelled task that *still*
  emitted `prompt eval time`. No live `llama-server`, no `/var/log` access.
- **AC2 — Per-release columns are asserted.** For every release the joiner
  reports: release reason, proxy release timestamp, joined
  `id_task` (or `unjoined`), whether a cancel was observed, the number of
  `prompt processing progress` lines after the cancel, the cancel→`stop
  processing` latency in seconds, and whether `prompt eval time` was emitted
  for that task.
- **AC3 — Unjoined is reported, never dropped.** A test asserts every release
  appears exactly once in the output, with unjoinable ones counted as
  `unjoined` and carrying a machine-readable reason; the sum of
  joined + unjoined equals the release count.
- **AC4 — No fabricated cancels.** A test asserts the joiner reports **no**
  cancel for shape (b), so a naive time-window join cannot pass by marking
  everything cancelled.
- **AC5 — Distributions are reported, not point estimates.** The cancel→`stop
  processing` latency is reported as p10/p50/p90, and tokens evaluated after
  the cancel are counted from the fixture's progress lines — not derived from
  `ABANDONED_PREFILL_RATE_TOK_S`.
- **AC6 — Test module runs green in isolation and in the suite.**
  `python -m pytest proxy/tests/test_abandoned_prefill_release_cancel.py`
  collects and (post-implementation) passes; the module needs no network, no
  GPU and no live proxy.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Add `proxy/tests/fixtures/abandoned_prefill_release_cancel_proxy.log` — real
   `local_eviction_after_acceptance` / `lease_released` / `abandoned_slot_recorded`
   line shapes (real field order, `slot_id=unknown`, `llama_task_id=unknown`).
2. Add `proxy/tests/fixtures/abandoned_prefill_release_cancel_llama.log` — real
   llama-server line shapes (`srv stop: cancel task, id_task = N`,
   `slot update_slots: … prompt processing progress, batch.n_tokens=…`,
   `slot release: … stop processing`, `prompt eval time = …`).
3. Write `proxy/tests/test_abandoned_prefill_release_cancel.py` importing the
   analyser the same way `proxy/tests/test_prefill_deadline_residual_analysis.py`
   does (add `proxy/scripts` to `sys.path`, `importlib.import_module`).
4. Keep every assertion on the *contract* (columns, invariants, distributions),
   not on internal helper names.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/tests/test_abandoned_prefill_release_cancel.py` — new test module.
- `proxy/tests/fixtures/abandoned_prefill_release_cancel_proxy.log` — new fixture.
- `proxy/tests/fixtures/abandoned_prefill_release_cancel_llama.log` — new fixture.
- `proxy/scripts/analyse_prefill_deadline_residual.py` — the module under test.
- `proxy/tests/test_prefill_deadline_residual_analysis.py` — the pattern to follow.

## Dependencies

None — this is the first (test-first) slice.

## Goal

Write the failing tests for the **corrected abandoned-prefill window model**
before changing it, so the 58/60 overlap figure and the 667 s median backlog
can be restated on a measured basis while staying backwards comparable.

Parent: LP-0MVVEQW5Y00962T2 — AC2, AC3 (measurement half).

## Target outcome

Tests that pin `abandoned_prefill_windows()` to the *observed* backend stop
(cancel → `slot release: … stop processing`) instead of
`tokens / ABANDONED_PREFILL_RATE_TOK_S`, including an explicit
"unbounded / legacy basis" fallback, dual-basis reporting, and the
zero-progress-while-draining count AC3's second half needs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Window end comes from the observed stop.** A test asserts that when
  a cancel→`stop processing` pair is available for a released dispatch, the
  window's `end` is the observed stop time (within tolerance) and its
  duration is **not** the token/rate estimate; the row records which basis
  produced it.
- **AC2 — Unbounded windows are labelled, not invented.** When no stop is
  observed, a test asserts the row is marked `bounded=false` and carries the
  legacy token/rate estimate explicitly labelled as an estimate — the two
  bases are never mixed silently.
- **AC3 — Dual-basis reporting.** The overlap count/total for
  `prefill_deadline` events (the 58/60 figure) is computed on **both** bases
  (legacy estimator and measured), both are present in the report, and the
  report states which one the verdict uses.
- **AC4 — A retry inside a cancelled-and-stopped window is not "starved".** A
  fixture where the retry dispatch starts *after* the observed stop yields
  `abandoned_prefill_overlap=false`; a fixture where it starts *before* the
  stop yields `true` — so the metric can no longer count post-stop dispatches
  as starved.
- **AC5 — Zero-progress while draining is counted.** The report exposes a
  count of accepted dispatches that expired their lease with no
  `prefill_progress_measured` while their session's slot was still inside an
  abandoned window — the second half of AC3, reported separately from the
  share.
- **AC6 — Hermetic and isolated.** `python -m pytest
  proxy/tests/test_abandoned_prefill_windows_measured.py` runs with no live
  logs; the existing suite test
  `proxy/tests/test_prefill_deadline_residual_analysis.py` keeps passing.

## Minimal Implementation

1. New fixture(s) under `proxy/tests/fixtures/` (or reuse of the sibling
   joiner fixture) with: measured stop present, stop absent, retry before stop,
   retry after stop, zero-progress lease inside a window.
2. `proxy/tests/test_abandoned_prefill_windows_measured.py` — table-driven
   assertions on `abandoned_prefill_windows()`, `backlog_evidence()` and the
   report keys.

   implementation item is free to refactor.

None (test-first). Sibling of the joiner test item; both feed the analyser
implementation item.

## Goal

Make every proxy release of an accepted local dispatch **attributable to a
backend task lifecycle**, and correct the abandoned-prefill window model, so
"prefills computed and thrown away" is a measurement rather than the
subtraction of two counters.

Parent: LP-0MVVEQW5Y00962T2 — AC2 (the instrument), with the model correction
AC1 needs and AC5's docstring requirement.

## Target outcome

`proxy/scripts/analyse_prefill_deadline_residual.py` (or a sibling module it
imports) joins `local_eviction_after_acceptance` / `lease_released` events to
`llama-server.log` task lifecycles over a ≥24 h restart-segmented window and
reports: releases with no explained backend stop (count + share), the
cancel→`stop processing` latency distribution, tokens evaluated after the
cancel, and unjoined releases. The abandoned-prefill windows are derived from
observed stops, with the legacy token/rate basis retained for comparability.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Release→cancel accounting exists and is produced from on-disk logs
  only.** A function (e.g. `release_cancel_accounting(...)`) emits, per
  window: `releases_total`, `releases_with_observed_cancel`,
  `releases_without_explained_backend_stop` (count and share),
  `releases_unjoined` (count and per-event reason), `cancel_to_stop_seconds`
  p10/p50/p90, and `tokens_evaluated_after_cancel` (totals and per-event).
- **AC2 — CLI exposure.** The script gains a documented way to point at the
  `llama-server` log(s) for a window (reusing/extending `--llama-log`) and
  emits the accounting in the JSON dataset; `--json` output stays
  machine-parseable and the text summary states the accounting headline.
- **AC3 — Nothing is dropped.** Every release appears exactly once: joined,
  unjoined-with-reason, or explained-by-another-mechanism. The sums are
  asserted by the sibling test item.
- **AC4 — Window model corrected, both bases kept.** `abandoned_prefill_windows()`
  derives each window's end from the observed backend stop when one exists and
  marks the row `bounded=true/false`; `ABANDONED_PREFILL_RATE_TOK_S` remains
  available as the legacy basis, and the report carries both the legacy and
  corrected overlap counts for `prefill_deadline` events (so 58/60 can be
  restated on both bases).
- **AC5 — Docstring tells the truth.** `abandoned_prefill_windows()`'s
  docstring no longer asserts "a released dispatch is **not** cancelled at
  `llama-server`"; it states what is measured, what is estimated, and the
  provenance of each constant.
- **AC6 — Tests from both test-first items pass**; `proxy/tests/test_prefill_deadline_residual_analysis.py`
  keeps passing unchanged; the full suite is green through `/skill:test`.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Parse `llama-server.log` lines into task-lifecycle records: `launch_slot_`
  (slot/task), `update_slots … prompt processing progress` (`n_tokens`,
  `batch.n_tokens`, `progress`), `srv stop: cancel task, id_task = N`,
  `slot release: … stop processing`, `prompt eval time`.
2. Join each release to a task by (a) `llama_task_id`/`slot_id` when the log
   line carries them, else (b) the session's slot at release + nearest
   preceding `launch_slot_` for that slot; record how each join was made and
   count the unjoined residue.
3. Emit the accounting block in `build_report()` and the text summary.
4. Re-point `abandoned_prefill_windows()` at observed stops, keeping the
   legacy estimate under an explicit `bounded=false` label, and have
   `backlog_evidence()`/`attribute_events()` report both bases.
5. Rewrite the `abandoned_prefill_windows()` docstring per AC5.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/scripts/analyse_prefill_deadline_residual.py` — the analyser
  (`abandoned_prefill_windows()`, `backlog_evidence()`, `build_report()`,
  `backend_prefill_accounting()`, `parse_args()`, `_text_summary()`).
- `proxy/tests/test_abandoned_prefill_release_cancel.py` — joiner tests.
- `proxy/tests/test_abandoned_prefill_windows_measured.py` — window-model tests.
- `proxy/tests/test_prefill_deadline_residual_analysis.py` — must stay green.
- `proxy/tests/fixtures/` — the fixture pair from the test-first item.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the two test-first items (joiner contract, window-model contract).

## Constraints

- Log-only measurement (no in-process counters), per
  `docs/dev/prefill-deadline-residual.md`.
- `llama-server.log` lines carry no wall-clock timestamp: the joiner must be
  valid only for a file that covers the analysed window, and must say so when
  it cannot establish coverage (same caveat as
  `backend_prefill_accounting()`).
- Do not change the *definition* of `EVICTION_REASONS_AFTER_ACCEPTANCE` or the
  eviction log line format here (that is the routing item's business).

## Goal

Decide, on ≥24 h of evidence, **which mechanism** actually wastes the prefill
compute and starves the retry — and publish the decision record so the fix is
chosen by evidence rather than by the intake premise.

Parent: LP-0MVVEQW5Y00962T2 — AC1 (the gate for the rest of the tree).

## Target outcome

A committed record at `docs/dev/abandoned-prefill-release-cancel.md` giving,
for a stated ≥24 h restart-segmented window: per-release release reason, proxy
release timestamp, joined backend task id (or `unjoined`), whether a cancel
was observed, `prompt processing progress` lines after the cancel, cancel→
`stop processing` seconds, and whether `prompt eval time` was emitted for that
task — plus an explicit verdict on **H1–H5** with the deciding log lines, the
26 % (285/1 092) and 58/60 figures confirmed or restated, and the chosen fix
mechanism for the starvation path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Window and provenance stated.** The record names the exact window
  (start/end, hours), the restart events inside it, the analyser command
  line(s) used, and commits the JSON dataset (or documents where it lives).
- **AC2 — Per-release evidence is tabulated against the AC2 targets.** For
  the window: releases with an observed backend cancel, releases without an
  explained backend stop (count and share, **compared against the parent AC2
  target of ≤ 5 %**, with the verdict stated), releases unjoined, the
  cancel→`stop processing` latency distribution (p10/p50/p90) with a
  **recorded p90 bound**, and tokens evaluated after the cancel — all produced
  by the analyser, not by hand.
- **AC3 — H1–H5 each get a verdict with the deciding lines.** H1 abandoned
  prefill runs to completion; H2 cancel lands at a batch boundary (tail
  bounded by `batch.n_tokens` at the measured prompt-eval rate); H3 the 26 %
  is an accounting artefact (reconcile `prompt eval time` against
  `Stream finished … provider=local` per hour **and** enumerate non-proxy
  `llama-server` consumers with counts); H4 the retry is queued behind a
  draining slot (`launch_slot_` of the retry vs the abandoned task's
  `slot release`, joined through session→slot affinity); H5 the residual is
  capacity, not starvation (event prompt size and measured prompt-eval rate
  against the 120 s deadline; whether any later dispatch of the same prompt
  reached `progress = 1.0`).
- **AC4 — The two headline figures are confirmed or restated on both bases.**
  The 26 % (285/1 092) abandoned-prefill share and the 58/60
  `prefill_deadline`-overlap share are stated on the legacy estimator basis
  **and** the corrected measured basis, with the difference explained. Neither
  figure is silently swapped.
- **AC5 — The Option D path is measured, not inherited.** The record states
  explicitly whether the releases in this window came from
  `MeasuredCacheAbortDetourError` (Option D) or the deadline path, and does
  **not** reuse the 42/82 cancel evidence taken on the deadline path as proof
  for Option D.
- **AC6 — A fix mechanism is chosen and justified.** The record ends with one
  chosen mechanism for the starvation path — (a) route the retry to a free
  slot, (b) hold the dispatch out of "about to prefill" pricing while the
  session's own abandoned work drains, or (c) bound the wait against the
  drain — with the evidence line that decides it, the alternatives rejected,
  and the risks. It also states whether a `-ub`/`--batch-size` change is
  warranted, and if so files a follow-up work item (linked) rather than
  tuning it here.
- **AC7 — Doc claims corrected where they are contradicted.** Claims in
  `proxy/docs/routing.md` and the analyser docstring that the evidence
  contradicts are recorded in the decision document (their full rewrite is the
  docs item's scope) so the contradiction cannot survive without a pointer.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Run the corrected analyser (`--start`/`--end`/`--llama-log-dir`) over the
   largest clean ≥24 h restart-segmented window available on disk.
2. Build the per-release table by joining proxy releases to backend task
   lifecycles; keep the unjoined residue visible.
3. Compute the H3 reconciliations (backend `prompt eval time`/hour vs proxy
   `Stream finished … provider=local`/hour; non-proxy consumers via `grep` over
   `proxy/scripts/`, benchmarks and health probes).
4. Compute the H4/H5 discriminators (retry `launch_slot_` time vs the
   abandoned task's `slot release`; prompt size vs `deadline / rate`;
   `progress = 1.0` occurrences per prompt cluster).
5. Write the record with the verdict table, the chosen mechanism, and the
   follow-up decision.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `docs/dev/abandoned-prefill-release-cancel.md` — the new decision record.
- `proxy/scripts/analyse_prefill_deadline_residual.py` — the instrument.
- `docs/dev/prefill-deadline-residual.md` — the method this record follows.
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` — the claims under test.
- `proxy/proxy/session.py` — `_slot_id_for_session` (session→slot affinity for
  the H4 join).

## Dependencies

Blocked by the analyser accounting item.

## Constraints

- Evidence comes from **on-disk logs only**, ≥24 h, restart-segmented.
- Out of scope (owned elsewhere): the 120 s prefill deadline, the 25 000-token
  cold budget, warmth pricing, slot count.
- Do not file the batch-size follow-up as a child of this item; it is a
  separate item linked from the record.

## Goal

Write the failing, hermetic tests for the starvation fix **before** the fix
exists, reproducing the shape the AC1 decision record identifies (a retry
re-dispatched into the slot the proxy itself just abandoned).

Parent: LP-0MVVEQW5Y00962T2 — AC3 (test-first half).

## Target outcome

A test module that reproduces the verified starvation shape with fake
`llama-server` behaviour and asserts the post-fix invariants, plus regression
guards proving the ordinary warm path is untouched.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — The defect is reproduced hermetically.** A test models: session S is
  pinned to slot 0 (`_slot_id_for_session`), the proxy releases S's dispatch
  early (deadline and `measured_cache_deficit` variants), the backend keeps
  slot 0 processing for a bounded drain, and S's retry is dispatched again to
  slot 0. Pre-fix, the retry expires its lease with
  `prefill_progress_measured=0` — the test asserts this shape is reproducible
  (xfail/marker is acceptable once, but the final form must assert the fixed
  behaviour).
- **AC2 — Fixed behaviour asserted (both halves of AC3).** With the fix:
  (a) the retry either is not admitted into a slot still draining its own
  abandoned work, or is routed to a free slot; and (b) **no** accepted
  dispatch expires its lease with zero `prefill_progress_measured` while its
  session's slot is draining abandoned work.
- **AC3 — The decision is observable.** Any release or refusal caused by the
  drain emits a distinct, attributable log line (asserted by field, e.g.
  `reason=`/`drain`/`abandoned` markers) so the post-change window can count
  it without guessing.
- **AC4 — No warm-path regression guard lost.** A test asserts that with **no**
  abandoned drain present, dispatch/admission behaviour and log lines are
  unchanged (no extra refusal, no extra detour, session keeps its warm slot).
- **AC5 — No duplication of the annotation work.** No test requires the fix to
  record slot identity itself; the module must pass whether
  `abandoned_slot_id` is populated by this item or by LP-0MVUVHAQP001IRKK.
- **AC6 — Isolated and fast.** `python -m pytest
  proxy/tests/test_abandoned_dispatch_starvation.py` runs with no live
  `llama-server`, no sleeps longer than ~1 s of fake time, and no network.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Reuse the fake-server/lease fixtures already present in
   `proxy/tests/test_abandoned_local_dispatch.py` and
   `proxy/tests/test_measured_cache_abort_wiring.py` rather than inventing a
   new harness.
2. Model the backend drain as a controllable "slot still processing until T"
   stub so the test controls the drain boundary exactly.
3. Drive the retry through the real dispatch helper(s) under test, not a
   re-implementation.
4. Keep assertions on observable behaviour and log fields.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/tests/test_abandoned_dispatch_starvation.py` — new test module.
- `proxy/tests/test_abandoned_local_dispatch.py` — reusable fixtures/patterns.
- `proxy/tests/test_measured_cache_abort_wiring.py` — downstream stubs.
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — `_release_unserved_dispatch`,
  `_record_abandoned_slot`, `_abandoned_slot_lookup`.
- `proxy/proxy/session.py` — `_slot_id_for_session`, `_slot_owners`.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the AC1 decision-record item: the test must reproduce the mechanism
the evidence chose, not a guessed one.

## Constraints

- Do not modify production code here beyond what is needed to make the module
  importable; the fix is the sibling implementation item.
- Do not re-test `abandoned_busy` status annotation (LP-0MVUTYHG7001S6BM).

## Goal

Remove the starvation path the AC1 evidence identified: an immediate retry
must never be admitted into a slot that is still draining work the proxy itself
abandoned without that fact being visible to admission and to the eviction log.

Parent: LP-0MVVEQW5Y00962T2 — AC3 (behaviour half).

## Target outcome

The mechanism chosen in `docs/dev/abandoned-prefill-release-cancel.md`
implemented as the smallest end-to-end change on the accepted-dispatch path,
with hermetic tests green and the warm path provably unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — The chosen mechanism is implemented.** Exactly one of: (a) route the
  retry to a free slot when its pinned slot is draining its own abandoned
  work; (b) hold the dispatch out of "about to prefill" pricing until the drain
  ends; (c) bound the wait against the drain before acceptance — as decided by
  the AC1 record, which the item cites in its description/comment.
- **AC2 — No zero-progress lease behind own abandoned drain.** In the hermetic
  scenario the retry either starts on a free slot or is refused before
  acceptance with an attributable reason; an accepted dispatch never expires
  with no `prefill_progress_measured` while its session's slot drains work the
  proxy abandoned.
- **AC3 — The drain state is visible where the decision is made.** Admission
  and the eviction log can both see it (a log field or reason on the release /
  refusal path). The item does **not** reimplement the abandoned-slot registry:
  it consumes `_abandoned_slot_lookup` / the published status annotation, or
  derives drain state from `/slots`; any identity gap found on the Option D
  path is reported to LP-0MVUVHAQP001IRKK, not fixed here.
- **AC4 — Warm path unchanged.** With no drain present, dispatch, pricing,
  session→slot affinity and the eviction/lease log lines are byte-comparable to
  the pre-change behaviour for the existing test suite
  (`proxy/tests/test_abandoned_local_dispatch.py`,
  `test_measured_cache_abort*.py`, `test_prefill_deadline*.py`,
  `test_measured_prefill_regression.py`).
- **AC5 — Nothing forbidden is re-tuned.** `local_prefill_deadline_seconds`,
  `local_cold_prefill_budget_tokens`, warmth pricing, slot count and the
  `llama-server` batch size are unchanged.
- **AC6 — Tests green.** The starvation test module from the sibling item
  passes, and the full suite passes via `/skill:test`.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Implement the AC1-chosen hook at the narrowest point (dispatch/slot
   selection or admission guard) — one function plus the call site.
2. Read the drain state from existing state (`_slot_owners` /
   `_abandoned_slot_lookup` / fresh `/slots` status), never from new counters.
3. Emit one attributable log line per decision taken because of a drain, using
   the existing line shapes (`lease_released …`, `local_dispatch_denied …`) and
   a stable reason token the analyser can count.
4. Update the affected code comments in place (full doc sweep is the docs
   item).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — dispatch/admission helpers,
  `_try_acquire_local_dispatch`, `_check_slot_availability`,
  `_abandoned_slot_lookup`.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — provider selection/admission guard call sites.
- `proxy/proxy/session.py` — `_slot_id_for_session` / `_slot_owners`.
- `proxy/proxy/admission_events.py` — eviction line fields if the drain state
  must appear there.
- `proxy/tests/test_abandoned_dispatch_starvation.py` — the tests it must pass.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the starvation test item (test-first) and, transitively, by the AC1
decision record that fixes the mechanism.

## Constraints

- Annotation ownership: `abandoned_slot_id`/registry completeness belongs to
  LP-0MVUTYHG7001S6BM / LP-0MVUVHAQP001IRKK. This item owns *behaviour*.
- No new config knob unless the AC1 record justifies one; prefer deriving from
  existing state.

## Goal

Produce the post-change ≥24 h evidence the closure verdict needs: the
abandoned-window share of `prefill_deadline` events falls from 58/60 to a
recorded target, no accepted dispatch starves behind its own abandoned drain,
and no warm-path or throughput regression appears against a matched pre-change
window.

Parent: LP-0MVVEQW5Y00962T2 — AC3 and AC4.

## Target outcome

A committed report (JSON dataset + Markdown record) covering both the
pre-change and post-change windows with deltas, produced by the corrected
analyser from on-disk logs, and the restart evidence proving the post-change
window ran the fixed build.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Restart evidence.** The report proves the proxy was restarted onto
  the fixed commit before the post-change window began (re-base/rotation event
  and the running build), because a window on the old build measures the old
  code (the LP-0MVVJYJQ9001I8QK failure mode).
- **AC2 — AC3 first half, both bases.** The share of `prefill_deadline` events
  whose dispatch start falls inside an abandoned-prefill window is reported
  for both the legacy and the measured basis, pre-change vs post-change, with
  the pre-change 58/60 baseline and the target (≤ 20 %, per the intake
  assumption) stated explicitly.
- **AC3 — AC3 second half.** The report counts accepted dispatches that
  expired with no `prefill_progress_measured` while their session's slot was
  still draining abandoned work: target zero, and any occurrence is listed
  individually with its session/slot/time so it can be triaged.
- **AC4 — Reason conversion is excluded.** `measured_cache_deficit` releases
  and their per-hour rate are reported alongside `prefill_deadline` for both
  windows, so a `prefill_deadline` reduction produced by reason conversion is
  visible rather than rewarded.
- **AC5 — AC4 no-regression, with deltas, not a verdict.** Against the matched
  pre-change window (diurnally comparable, stated boundaries): local
  completions per hour, large-warm completion latency p50/p90, and
  `measured_cache_deficit` releases per hour, each with its numeric delta and
  the direction required by AC4.
- **AC6 — Method is reproducible.** Window boundaries, restart segmentation,
  the exact analyser command lines, and the committed dataset file(s) are
  recorded; the numbers in the prose are traceable to the JSON.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Pick the matched pre-change window (already-measured baseline from
   `docs/dev/prefill-deadline-residual.md`, ideally diurnally matched) and the
   post-change ≥24 h window starting after the restart onto the fix.
2. Run the corrected analyser for both windows; commit both JSON datasets
   under `docs/dev/`.
3. Extract local completions/hour and large-warm completion latency p50/p90
   for both windows with the existing measurement route
   (`docs/dev/measured-prefill-capture.md`), plus
   `measured_cache_deficit`/h.
4. Write the report with both windows, the deltas, and the per-event list of
   any zero-progress starvations.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `docs/dev/prefill-deadline-residual.md` — method and the pre-change baseline.
- `docs/dev/measured-prefill-capture.md` — warm-path measurement route.
- `docs/dev/abandoned-prefill-release-cancel.md` — the mechanism decision.
- `proxy/scripts/analyse_prefill_deadline_residual.py` — the instrument.
- `docs/dev/prefill-deadline-residual-*.json` — dataset naming convention.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the starvation fix item, and by the fix actually being deployed and
the proxy restarted (Operational precondition, recorded as a blocker if the
restart has not happened when this item starts).

## Constraints

- Log-only, on-disk measurement; ≥24 h windows; restart-segmented.
- If the post-change window cannot be collected (no restart yet), record the
  blocker and do not substitute a shorter window silently.
- Do not re-tune anything to make the numbers land.

## Goal

Leave the three records and the code comments consistent with the measured
behaviour, so no document still claims "a released dispatch is not cancelled at
`llama-server`" or a backlog figure the evidence does not support.

Parent: LP-0MVVEQW5Y00962T2 — AC5 (documentation half).

## Target outcome

`proxy/docs/routing.md`, `docs/dev/prefill-deadline-residual.md`,
`docs/dev/measured-prefill-capture.md` and the `abandoned_prefill_windows()`
docstring describe the same measured behaviour, cross-link the decision record,
and carry the restated figures on both bases.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — `proxy/docs/routing.md` (abandoned dispatch section).** States what
  the release does to the backend on **each** release path, including the
  Option D (`MeasuredCacheAbortDetourError`) path's plumbing status, with the
  measured evidence cited from `docs/dev/abandoned-prefill-release-cancel.md`
  rather than the superseded 42/82 deadline-path figure presented as generic.
- **AC2 — `docs/dev/prefill-deadline-residual.md`.** The abandoned-prefill
  contributing-mechanism section states the measured behaviour, restates the
  58/60 overlap on both the legacy and corrected bases, and points at the new
  decision record.
- **AC3 — `docs/dev/measured-prefill-capture.md`.** Any baseline the change
  moved is updated in place with its window and provenance (no silent
  substitution: the previous value stays visible where comparability matters).
- **AC4 — Analyser docstrings and code comments.** `abandoned_prefill_windows()`
  and any comment asserting the old model are consistent with the measured
  behaviour and the retained legacy basis; the constant
  `ABANDONED_PREFILL_RATE_TOK_S` documents what it is still used for.
- **AC5 — No contradictory claim survives.** A `grep` sweep for the removed
  claims (e.g. "not** cancelled at ``llama-server``", "prefill runs to
  completion") returns nothing outside historical/decision records, and the
  sweep command is recorded in the work item.
- **AC6 — Cross-links resolve.** The new decision record, the residual
  measurement, `routing.md` and the analyser docstring link to each other and
  to the work-item ids they depend on (LP-0MVRMI5HK00558TB,
  LP-0MVR7IN0O000DPXN, LP-0MVT2KSN3007QYFK, LP-0MVUTYHG7001S6BM,
  LP-0MVUVHAQP001IRKK).

## Minimal Implementation

1. Gather the measured statements from the decision record and the post-change
   measurement item.
2. Edit the three records and the analyser docstrings in one pass so they agree.
3. Run the grep sweep for removed claims; record it.
4. Add cross-links in both directions.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/docs/routing.md` — abandoned dispatch section (~line 2043 onward).
- `docs/dev/prefill-deadline-residual.md` — contributing-mechanism section.
- `docs/dev/measured-prefill-capture.md` — baselines and post-deploy figures.
- `docs/dev/abandoned-prefill-release-cancel.md` — the decision record.
- `proxy/scripts/analyse_prefill_deadline_residual.py` — docstrings and
  constants.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the AC1 decision record (facts) and the post-change measurement
(figures).

## Constraints

- Documentation only: no behaviour, knob or test changes here.
- Preserve the historical/decision record of what was believed before; mark
  superseded claims as superseded rather than deleting the history.
